text: . Indian Judoka Asmita Dey and Harsh Singh created history by winning the historic Commonwealth Gold Medal at Glasgow today. Asmita Dey clinched country’s first-ever Commonwealth Games Judo gold, defeating Canada’s Heidi Quach 2-1 in the women’s 48kg final. After the match was tied 1-1 at the end of regulation, Asmita secured a decisive Yuko with a leg tangle into the golden score period, sealing a memorable victory in extra time.In  Mens 60kg event, Harsh Singh secured gold medal after beating Joshua Katz of Australia in the final. A brilliant half-arm throw in the final minute earns him a Waza-ari sealing India’s second consecutive judo gold in Glasgow.India’s medal tally at the Commonwealth Games has risen to 19, including five gold, nine silver and five bronze medals.

. President Droupadi Murmu has congratulated athlete Tejaswin Shankar on winning the Bronze Medal in the Decathlon at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games 2026. In a social media post, the President described the achievement as a historic first for Indian athletics, as Tejaswin Shankar has become the first Indian to win a Commonwealth Games medal in the decathlon. The President expressed confidence that he will continue to scale new heights of success and bring greater glory to the country.Meanwhile, Prime Minister Narendra Modi has congratulated Tejaswin Shankar on winning the Bronze Medal in the Men’s Decathlon at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games 2026. In a social media post, the Prime Minister Mo lauded Tejaswin Shankar for delivering an exceptional all-round performance across all ten events of the decathlon. He congratulated the athlete on his historic achievement and wished him continued success in the years ahead.

. The Maldives has launched real-time cross-border fund transfers to India through the integration of its instant payment system, Favara, with India’s Unified Payments Interface (UPI). The Maldives Monetary Authority announced the successful rollout of the service yesterday, describing it as a major step in strengthening digital financial connectivity and economic cooperation between the two countries. The Finance Ministry said that under the new facility, individuals in the Maldives can transfer money in real time to beneficiaries in India.It added that transactions are initiated in Maldivian Rufiyaa and are credited directly in Indian Rupees to UPI-enabled bank accounts. In the initial phase, the service is available to customers of Bank of Maldives Plc and Maldives Islamic Bank Plc. Users can make person-to-person transfers through their mobile banking applications using the Favara payment platform.The Ministry said that permitted remittance categories include family-maintenance-related remittances under both Foreign Inward and Foreign Outward Remittance, as well as gift-related remittances permitted under Foreign Outward Remittance.The Ministry said that the implementation reflects close collaboration between the MMA, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), NPCI International Payments Limited (NIPL), participating financial institutions, and other stakeholders in both countries.

. In the Indian bullion market, 24 carat Gold was trading 0.4 per cent down at 1,43,500 rupees per 10 grams, while Silver was trading 1.1 per cent down at 2,17,930  rupees per kilogram, a short while ago.On the Multi Commodity Exchange, Gold for the August contract was trading nearly one per cent down at 1,41,869 rupees per 10 grams, and Silver for the September contract was trading 1.2 per cent down at 2,17,309 rupees per kilogram, when reports last came in.

. The Delhi Government has extended the deadline for the mandatory use of the Pink Saheli Smart Card for availing the free travel facility in its buses till the 16th of this month. Under revised decision, the conductors will continue issuing pink tickets till 15th of August. Delhi Transport Minister Dr Pankaj Kumar Singh said, the decision has been taken to facilitate a smooth transition to the smart card-based system and ensure that no eligible commuter is inconvenienced during the changeover. He directed all concerned officials, depot managers, regional managers and conductors to intensify public awareness campaigns and assist women passengers in obtaining their Pink Saheli Smart Cards well before the revised deadline. Dr Singh has also directed officials to ensure that no woman commuter is wrongly denied free travel under the existing arrangement up till 15th of this month. The Delhi Government informed that as of today, a total of 17 lakh 4 thousand fourty two Pink Cards have already been issued, reflecting the strong response from women commuters towards the initiative.

. India’s Unnati Hooda and Tanvi Sharma advanced to the Women’s Singles Semifinals of the Taipei Open today with impressive victories in their respective quarterfinals. Unnati secured a straight-game win over compatriot Devika Sihag by 23-21, 21-16 to book her place in the last four. Tanvi on the other hand, defeated Thailand’s Supanida Katethong 21-15, 18-21, 21-14 in a three-game contest.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall over East Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Coastal Karnataka, South Interior Karnataka, Konkan, Goa, Kerala and Mahe today. IMD also predicted heavy rainfall over Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Punjab, Haryana, Chandigarh, Delhi, West Rajasthan, Bihar, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep and some parts of Northeast India. The weather has forecast thunderstorm accompanied with lightning over Gujarat, Chhattisgarh, Vidarbha, Assam, and Tripura for today.

. The government has said that there are no dues pertaining to any of the States and Union Territories are pending under Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) Scheme till date. Minister of State for Rural Development Kamlesh Paswan said in reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha that the Viksit Bharat-G RAM G) Act, 2025 came into force with effect from 1st of this month in rural areas of the entire country. He said, all States and UTs have notified the VB G RAM G Scheme and have started implementing it.Mr Paswan said, the Government continuously monitors the implementation of the VB-G RAM G Scheme through the Management Information System, regular review meetings and other appropriate mechanisms. The Minister added that the budgetary allocation of over 95 thousand crore rupees has been made for the Scheme during the Financial  year 2026-27. He added that this is among the largest ever allocation made at the Budget Estimate Stage for any rural employment scheme in the history of the country.

. President Droupadi Murmu has given assent to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026. The bill was passed by Parliament on Thursday. The Act aims to curb unfair practices in public examinations by introducing stricter punishments and establishing fast-track courts.It seeks to strengthen transparency, fairness, and integrity in the examination system by creating a robust legal framework while protecting the future of students. The Act includes several key provisions, including stringent penalties such as imprisonment of up to ten years, fines of up to ten crore rupees, and the confiscation of properties belonging to convicted offenders.To ensure speedy disposal of cases, the Act requires every state government and union territory administration to establish special fast-track courts for day-to-day trials. It also mandates that investigations into offences must be completed within two months from the date of registration of information at a police station, while trials must be concluded within three months from the filing of the chargesheet.

. Hundreds of migrants have entered Spain’s North African enclave of Ceuta from Morocco over the past week, overwhelming local resources, regional leader Juan Jesús Vivas said yesterday.Mr. Vivas called on Spain’s government to intervene, warning of a humanitarian and security emergency. Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska is expected to visit Ceuta today.Spanish authorities said migrants reached the enclave by swimming, using flotation devices and crossing through a gate in the border fence. Spain said it is working with Morocco to curb the crossings and return those who entered illegally.

. In Commonwealth Games, Indian Weightlifter Lovepreet Singh won a silver medal in the men’s 110 kg category while Seema Kaliramna bagged a bronze medal in women’s discus throw at Glasgow last night. Australia continued to lead the standings with 110 medals while India were 10th with 17 medals on Day 8. India’s medal count includes three gold, 10 silver and four bronze.India’s Lovepreet set the Games record in snatch and narrowly missed out on the gold medal. Lovepreet lifted a Games record 176kg in the snatch before managing 212kg in the clean and jerk for a total of 388kg. New Zealand’s David Liti won gold with 389kg while England’s Andrew Griffiths took the bronze medal with a total of 356kg.In women’s discus throw, Seema Kaliramna clinched a bronze medal with 58.65 meter while compatriot Nidhi Rani finished fourth. Jamaica’s Samantha Hall won the gold with a Games-leading throw of 61.66 meter, while Canada’s Julia Tunks took silver with 60.67 meter.Earlier in the day, Neeraj Chopra qualified for men’s javelin throw finals. Javelin throwers Rohit Yadav and Yashvir Singh have also entered the finals. Neeraj finished fifth, Rohit Yadav 9th and Yashvir Singh 10th in the qualification round.Two Indian triple jumpers, Praveen Chithravel and Selva Prabhu Thirumaran advanced to the final. Tejaswin Shankar also remained in medal contention in the men’s decathlon, ending the opening day in second place with 4,339 points after five events.

. President Droupadi Murmu today interacted with a group of grassroots innovators from the Atal Innovation Mission at Rashtrapati Bhavan and witnessed their innovations in an exhibition. During the meeting, the President emphasised that grassroots innovations are well-suited to society’s needs, as they combine local experience, scientific thinking, and individual creativity with a sense of social responsibility. President Murmu also appreciated the efforts of the innovators for working with conviction despite challenges to bring about positive change in the lives of individuals, families, and communities.

. The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) has facilitated the first-ever air shipment of Neelam and Totapuri mangoes from Karnataka to the Maldives. The Ministry of Commerce and Industry has said, the mango export initiative delivers over 50 per cent higher returns to farmers compared to conventional market channels. It added that the export marks a significant milestone in promoting Karnataka’s late-season mango varieties in international markets and further strengthening India’s mango export basket.Neelam mango is widely appreciated for its sweet, juicy pulp, rich aroma and suitability for desserts, smoothies and beverages, while Totapuri mango is known for its distinctive shape, sweet-tangy flavour and versatility for both fresh consumption and processing. Harvested from late June to the end of July, these late-season varieties offer an opportunity to extend India’s mango export season and cater to international demand beyond the peak harvest period.

. At the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, India delivered another outstanding performance yesterday, clinching two historic gold medals in Judo, securing a memorable double podium finish in the Men’s Javelin Throw, winning a first-ever bronze medal in the Decathlon, and booking places for 10 boxers in their respective finals.Judokas Asmita Dey and Harsh Singh scripted history by becoming India’s first-ever Commonwealth Games gold medallists in the sport. Asmita clinched the women’s 48-kilogram title after defeating Canada’s Heidi Quach in the golden score, while Harsh defeated Australian Olympian Joshua Katz to win the yellow metal in Men’s 60-kilogram category. Yamini Mourya added a silver in the women’s 57-kilogram event, giving India its best-ever Commonwealth Games campaign in judo with two gold and one silver medal.In Athletics, Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra won silver in the men’s javelin throw with a season-best effort of 85.83 metres. Sri Lanka’s Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage claimed gold with a throw of 89.75 metres, while India’s Yashvir Singh secured bronze with a personal-best effort of 85.41 metres on his final attempt. Tejaswin Shankar also created history by becoming the first Indian to win a Commonwealth Games medal in the decathlon, claiming bronze.India’s boxers also delivered an outstanding performance, with 10 pugilists winning their respective semi-final bouts to enter the finals. They are : Sakshi Chaudhary in Women’s 51 kg, Preeti Pawar in Women’s 54kg, Jaismine Lamboria in Women’s 57 kg, Priya Ghanghas in Women’s 60kg, Arundhati Choudhary in Women’s 70 kg and Lovlina Borgohain in Women’s 75kg, Jadumani Singh in Men’s 55kg, Sachin Siwach in Men’s 60kg, Ankush Panghal in Men’s 80kg and Narender Berwal in Men’s 90(Plus) kg.In lawn bowls, Navneet Singh and Dinesh Kumar registered their fourth consecutive victory in the Men’s Pairs event, while Nayanmoni Saikia won her women’s singles match. However, it was a disappointing outing for India’s cyclists. Dinesh Kumar and Harshveer Singh Sekhon failed to qualify for the men’s 4,000-metre individual pursuit, while no Indian rider advanced in the men’s keirin event.India is currently placed 10th in the overall medal standings with 23 medals-five gold, 12 silver and six bronze. Australia continues to top the table with 128 medals, including 55 gold.

. The government has debunked a video circulating on social media claiming that Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has promoted an investment scheme promising easy monetary benefits. The Fact Check Unit of the Press Information Bureau (PIB) informed that the video is fake and has been created using Artificial Intelligence.The Unit added that the Finance Minister has not endorsed any such investment scheme or platform. PIB said that fraudsters frequently use AI-generated content and false promises of extraordinary returns to deceive the public. It further urged the citizens to always verify such claims through official sources before investing money or sharing their personal or financial information.

. Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri concluded his two-day official visit to Bhutan yesterday. During his visit, Mr Misri co-chaired the fifth India-Bhutan Development Cooperation Talks for the 13th Five Year Plan of Bhutan. During the 5th Plan Talks, both sides reviewed the overall progress and implementation of Government of India’s support of 10 thousand crore rupees for Bhutan’s 13th Five Year Plan. A total of 12 new Project Tied Assistance, PTA projects amounting to 332 crore rupees were approved. They cover sectors such as infrastructure, healthcare, agriculture, urban amenities and disaster management.The Foreign Secretaries also witnessed the exchange of the Umbrella Line of Credit Agreement between the Bhutan government and EXIM Bank of India to operationalise a concessional Line of Credit of 4000 crore rupees for energy projects in Bhutan. They also witnessed the signing of MoU between All India Institute of Medical Sciences, New Delhi and Khesar Gyalpo University of Medical Science of Bhutan for collaboration on research and exchange programmes on health-related education and training.Foreign Secretary Misri received an audience with Bhutan King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuk. He also called on Prime Minister Tshering Tobgay and Foreign Affairs and External Trade Minister Lyonpo D.N. Dhungyel. The two sides discussed all aspects of bilateral cooperation including development partnership, energy, trade and investment, connectivity, people-to-people ties, as well as other regional issues of mutual importance. The Bhutanese side appreciated the support from India and its significance for wide-ranging programmes under its 13th FYP.Our correspondent reports that India and Bhutan share an exemplary partnership characterised by trust, goodwill and mutual understanding at all levels and close people-to-people contacts.

. Global crude oil prices rose today. Brent crude was trading 1.4 per cent up at 90 US dollars and 25 cents per barrel in intra-day trade. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 2.6 per cent up at 85 US dollars and 77 cents per barrel, when reports last came in.

. In U17 World Championships, Indian wrestler Nikita Sehrawat settled for a silver medal while Kamna Babal and Garima bagged bronze medals in the women’s event in Baku, Azerbaijan yesterday. In 57 kg category final, Nikita suffered a 0-6 defeat to Epenesa Elison of the USA. In the 49 kg category, Kamna Babal defeated Russia’s Irina Tsydeeva 3-2 in the third-place play-off match. In the 73kg bronze medal match, Garima defeated Spain’s Paula Benaixa Perez by technical superiority.

. The Ministry of Tourism and IndiGo have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) today, marking the beginning of a strategic collaboration to promote Incredible India Initiative. In a social media post, Union Culture and Tourism Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat said that India has an extraordinary tourism story to tell, and under this partnership both the Government and IndiGo together are we are taking it to the world. He noted that the MoU marks the beginning of Incredible India by IndiGo, a strategic partnership that will leverage IndiGo’s extensive global network to showcase country’s unparalleled cultural, spiritual, natural and wellness destinations to millions of travelers worldwide.Mr Shekhawat underlined that this collaboration is another step towards strengthening Brand India and making the nation a preferred global tourism destination under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

. Union Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia today reviewed the progress of the Bharat 6G Alliance (B6GA) in New Delhi and reiterated the government’s commitment to making India a global leader in 6G technologies. The review focused on the progress made by the Bharat 6G Alliance towards achieving Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of making India a front-line contributor in the design, development and deployment of 6G technology by 2030. The Alliance is working through seven specialised groups covering areas such as spectrum, technology, applications, sustainability, manufacturing, outreach and 6G use cases.On the occasion, Mr Scindia stressed the need to benchmark India’s 6G progress against global developments and strengthen collaboration among the Alliance’s working groups. He emphasised that India’s 6G journey must be driven by indigenous research, global standards participation, domestic manufacturing and strong partnerships among government, industry, academia, startups and research institutions.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will be on a day-long visit to Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka today. Mr Modi will first travel to Andhra Pradesh, where he will lay the foundation stone, inaugurate and dedicate to the nation multiple development projects worth nearly 18,000 crore rupees at Bhogapuram in Vizianagaram district.The Prime Minister will inaugurate the Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram. The new Greenfield airport has been built under the Public-Private Partnership mode at a cost of over 5600 crore rupees. It has been designed to handle 6 million passengers annually. The airport is expected to provide a significant boost to tourism, trade, investment and employment generation in the state while strengthening air connectivity in the region.The Prime Minister will lay the foundation stone of the ASIP Semiconductor Project at Visakhapatnam, being developed with an investment of over 460 crore rupees. It is Andhra Pradesh’s first semiconductor manufacturing facility approved under the India Semiconductor Mission. The facility will manufacture around 96 million semiconductor chips annually and create high-skilled employment opportunities, while also fostering a robust ancillary ecosystem to support semiconductor manufacturing.Mr Modi will also lay the foundation stone for the Transmission System for Integration of Kurnool-IV Renewable Energy Zone – Phase-I 4.5 Gigawatt, being implemented by PowerGrid through a Special Purpose Vehicle, with an investment of about 5,550 crore rupees.The Prime Minister will inaugurate the Transmission System for Kurnool Wind Energy Zone and Solar Energy Zone (Andhra Pradesh) – Part A and Part B, implemented at a cost of around 3550 crore rupees. He will also inaugurate Transmission Scheme for Solar Energy Zone in Ananthapuram 2500 Megawatt and Kurnool 1,000 Megawatt, implemented by Powergrid at a cost of over 800 crore rupees. These transmission projects will enable the evacuation of power generated from the renewable energy zones in Kurnool and Ananthapuram and the transmission of power to beneficiaries across the country through the National Grid.Mr Modi will also dedicate to the nation and lay the foundation stone of National Highway projects worth over 1880 crore rupees. He will also lay the foundation stone of the high-level bridge at Lingasamudram on the Penchalakona-Yerpedu section of National Hightway-565. These projects will ease congestion in Vijayawada and several other cities, improve road safety, reduce travel distance and travel time between Visakhapatnam and Hyderabad, and promote regional connectivity.After concluding his visit to Andhra Pradesh, the prime minister will reach Mysuru in Karnataka, where he will inaugurate the Swami Vivekananda Cultural Youth Centre – Viveka Smaraka. Mr Modi will also address the gathering on the occasion. The Viveka Smaraka commemorates Swami Vivekananda’s historic visit to Mysuru in November 1892 during his journey across India.Established at the historic Niranjana Math, the Viveka Smaraka is spread across a built-up area of over 81 thousand square feet and comprises a main building and an annex block. It houses a 4-D Experience Centre, an exhibition hall, an amphitheatre with a seating capacity of around 700 people, classrooms, conference rooms, a library, a reading room, a meditation and yoga hall, and a book stall. The centre also includes dedicated facilities for students preparing for competitive examinations.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that abuse and hatred never solve anything. He appealed for compassion toward misguided youth who have gone astray, saying they should be guided onto the right path in the spirit of nation-building and national interest, rather than punished.In a video message posted on his social media handles, the Prime Minister referred to the recent incident at Jantar Mantar in the National Capital, where abusive language was used against him and his late mother. He said the episode had been witnessed by people across the country and the world, adding that while the anger and disappointment in society over such conduct were understandable, childhood is also a phase of learning, making mistakes and correcting them.Mr Modi said, instead of dragging such youngsters through court proceedings or subjecting them to social harassment, society should embrace them and show them the right path. He said he wished to forgive the children involved and appealed to people to accept the same spirit of compassion and understanding.Emphasising the importance of guidance over punishment, the Prime Minister said young people who lose their way need support and positive direction so they can become responsible citizens.Addressing the youth, Prime Minister Modi urged them to learn from their mistakes, move forward with confidence and dedicate themselves to nation-building. He said India is progressing rapidly and expressed the hope that every young person would also advance in life by pursuing their dreams and contributing to the country’s development.Calling upon citizens to work together for the nation, the Prime Minister reiterated his message that abuse and hatred cannot resolve problems.

. Government e Marketplace (GeM) today launched the 10-day celebrations ahead of its 10th Foundation Day. The event also witnessed the unveiling of the official GeM 10th Foundation Day logo, symbolising a decade of its journey in building India’s trusted digital public procurement ecosystem. Addressing the gathering, Chief Executive Officer of GeM, Mihir Kumar, reflected on the organisation’s transformative journey over the past ten years and outlined its vision for the next phase of growth, innovation and stakeholder-centric public procurement.The Ministry of Commerce and Industry said, the launch of the celebrations marks the beginning of a year-long series of stakeholder engagement initiatives and outreach programmes across the country. The Ministry noted that GeM will also organise a Buyer Meet on 5th and a Seller Roundtable on 10th of the next month. The occasion will honour distinguished buyers and sellers for their exemplary contributions to strengthening the GeM ecosystem.

. Indian boxers continued their impressive run at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, with five pugilists securing places in the finals today. Preeti Pawar, Ankush Panghal, Jaismine Lamboria, Arundhati Chaudhary and Jadumani Singh advanced to the title bouts in their respective categories, assuring the country of at least four Silver Medals. Preeti entered the final with a unanimous 5-nil victory over Zambia’s Catherine Mwape in Women’s 54kg Semifinal. She will take on Canada’s Scarlett Delgado in the final tomorrow.Ankush Panghal entered the Men’s 80kg final defeating Canada’s Joshua Ofori by a unanimous 5:nil decision in the semi final. Jaismine Lamboria produced a dominant performance to storm into the women’s 57kg final as she defeated Lesotho’s Rapelang Maselela via Referee Stop Contest (RSC) in the semifinal.Arundhati reached women’s 70 kg final, after defeating Wales’ Rosie Eccles on a 4-nil split decision in the Semifinal. While, in the men’s 55 kg bout, Jadumani Singh outplayed Philip Haoseb of Namibia 5-nil in the semi-final. He will face Jye Dixon of Australia tomorrow for the gold medal. India have won 17 medals so far at the Commonwealth Games 2026, comprising three gold, nine silver and five bronze.

. Rajya Sabha has passed the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026. The bill will further amend the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971. The proposed legislation seeks to give Vande Mataram the same statutory protection as the national anthem, Jana Gana Mana. These offences are punishable with imprisonment up to three years, a fine, or both.Replying to a discussion on the Bill, Minister of State for Home Nityanand Rai said, the amendment in the Bill is not merely a legislative change. He said, it reflects the collective commitment to the soul of India, national consciousness, cultural heritage, and the ideals of the freedom struggle.The Minister said, in 1971, through the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, provisions were made to ensure respect for the National Flag, the Constitution, and the National Anthem, Jana Gana Mana. Mr Rai said, the deliberate insult of Vande Mataram will be punishable in the same manner as provided under the existing law. The National Song Vande Mataram was composed in 1875 by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay. The Minister claimed that in 1935, when Jawaharlal Nehru became the President of the Congress, he limited Vande Mataram to only two stanzas. On the other hand, in 1928, when Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose was Congress President, he requested Timir Baran Banerjee to prepare a complete and dignified musical version of the song. He said, on 15th August 1947, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel had asked Pandit Omkarnath Thakur to render the complete Vande Mataram on All India Radio at 6:30 in the morning, marking the beginning of the first Independence Day.The Minister said, on 24th January 1950, Dr. Rajendra Prasad stated in the Constituent Assembly that Vande Mataram, which holds historic importance in India’s freedom struggle, would be accorded the same respect as Jana Gana Mana. Mr Rai said opposing Vande Mataram reflects a policy of appeasement that undermines the nation’s pride.Earlier, initiating the discussion, BJP MP Dr Radha Mohan Das Agrawal said that for the past 123 years, Vande Mataram song had been disrespected. He stated that inspired by this song, the revolutionaries of the country made sacrifices for the nation. Mr Agrawal alleged that in 1923, during a Congress session, the then President of the Congress had insulted Vande Mataram.Golla Baburao of YSRCP requested all the Members of this House to uphold and respect the national song. He expressed his gratitude to the Government for introducing this Bill. Mr Baburao said that Vande Mataram is not just a song, but a source of inspiration that motivated countless freedom fighters to sacrifice their lives for the nation. He said, the spirit generated by this song played a significant role in the country’s struggle for independence. Sulata Deo of BJD, Sanjay Singh of AAP, Dr M Thambidurai of AIADMK, among others, participated in the discussion.After the passing of the Bill, the Upper House took up Special Mentions, where Members raised issues of urgent importance. After that, Rajya Sabha was adjourned till 11 AM tomorrow.

. Major US indices rallied yesterday, led by gains in chip stocks. The Nasdaq Composite Index jumped 2.8 per cent, ending a six-day losing streak. The S&P 500 rose almost 1.7 per cent and the Dow Jones Industrial Average settled 1.2 per cent higher.Meanwhile, the US economy grew at a slower pace in the second quarter this year. According to the advance estimate released by the US Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA), real gross domestic product increased at an annual rate of 1.5 per cent, down from 2.1 per cent in the first quarter.A separate report by the BEA showed that personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index rose 3.7 per cent in June on an annual basis, easing from a 4.1 per cent increase in May. On a monthly basis, it contracted by 0.1 per cent, from a rise of 0.5 per cent in May.

. External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar spoke to his Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi last evening and conveyed India’s deep concerns over the ongoing hostilities in the West Asia region. During the telephonic conversation, Dr Jaishankar strongly urged that attacks on commercial shipping and seafarers be avoided under any circumstance. He stressed that India condemns any such attack by any party. The External Affairs Minister said in a social media post that he was also apprised of Iran’s perspective of current developments and discussions, which are underway. He said India is always supportive of dialogue and diplomacy.

. Social media company Meta’s global team, which has been summoned by the Centre after it restricted Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Facebook post, will be questioned on issues around algorithmic bias and their role in public order. Official sources told Akashvani News that Meta’s global team is expected to be questioned sometime in the middle of next week. Meta will be asked to clarify issues around algorithmic bias, how their algorithm operates, and the company’s role in public order. The team will also appear before a parliamentary panel.The move assumes significance, as the government earlier this week summoned a top Meta executive after Prime Minister Modi’s recent post addressing India’s youth and promising stringent measures against paper leaks was briefly restricted on Facebook. While Meta attributed the incident to a technical glitch and apologised, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology found the explanation inadequate.

. A US computer science professor has been awarded 528,137 dollars in funding from the National Science Foundation for a research project being carried out in collaboration with India’s Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) to develop advanced technologies for precision soyabean breeding. It will run from October 2026 to September 2029.The project aims to build an AI-powered system to improve soybean breeding and farming. Researchers will use smart sensors, wireless networks, drone data and artificial intelligence to monitor crops, soil and weather conditions. The technology will help farmers tackle pests, diseases and changing climate conditions.The project includes researchers from universities and agricultural institutes in both the US and India, including IIT Delhi and the Indian Council of Agricultural Research. Officials say the research could support better crop varieties, improve food security and strengthen India-US scientific cooperation.
. In the forex market today, the rupee appreciated by 29 paise to end at 95 rupees and 39 paise against the US dollar.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke with the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, Andy Burnham, and congratulated him on assuming office. In a social media post yesterday, Mr Modi said, during their conversation they agreed to work together across sectors such as Technology, Innovation, Defence, Security, Clean Energy, Education and people-to-people ties and take the India-UK Comprehensive Strategic Partnership to new heights. He added that both nations will also collaborate closely to fully harness the trade and investment opportunities presented by the recently operationalized India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement, for the shared prosperity and well-being of people of India and UK. The Prime Minister also conveyed his best wishes to his UK counterpart for a successful tenure.

. The Union Cabinet has approved an expanded Khelo India Scheme and enhanced Assistance to National Sports Federations (ANSFs) with a combined outlay of 36,441 crore rupees for the period 2026-27 to 2030-31. Addressing media in New Delhi yesterday, Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said, the decision reaffirms the Government’s commitment to harnessing the power of sports for youth development and nation-building. He said it will ensure every talented youth to get a clear pathway to excellence. Mr Vasihanw said that the scheme will help build pan-India training facilities from grassroots to the Target Podium Olympic Scheme level.

. Italy has temporarily suspended open-border travel with Spain following a sharp rise in migrant crossings into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta from Morocoo. The move will affect flights and maritime transport, and temporarily suspend Spain’s Schengen border-free travel arrangements, which allow people to move freely across 29 European countries.Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani announced the decision yesterday, saying the temporary suspension of the Schengen agreement with Spain was needed to safeguard Italy’s security and protect the European Union’s external borders. According to Tajani, the measure became necessary after thousands of migrants crossed into Ceuta from Morocco. He said the move is permitted under European Union rules and will remain in force for one month from today.Meanwhile, more than 48,000 migrants have returned to Morocco from Ceuta, where around 60,000 people arrived in recent days. Spain and Morocco have agreed to strengthen measures to facilitate the swift return of all migrants who entered Ceuta illegally. Spanish Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska said both countries are committed to implementing the necessary steps to manage the situation and restore border control.

. The Department of Financial Services (DFS) has launched India’s first sovereign-backed Protection and Indemnity insurance product under Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool (BMIP). Addressing the launch event in New Delhi today, DFS Secretary Sanjay Lohiya congratulated all stakeholders involved in the process of formulation of the insurance product for achieving this milestone for India’s maritime sector.  He also handed over the first Protection and Indemnity policy document to Shipping Corporation of India Limited.The Ministry of Finance said with the introduction of BMIP, the war risk premium rates have decreased approximately by 35-40 percent, from the levels observed at the height of West Asia conflict.  It added that as of yesterday a total of 1 thousand 608 policies covering Cargo War risks and Hull War risks have been issued under the Pool. The Ministry noted that the BMIP mechanism ensures the continuity of maritime war risk insurance coverage, fosters the development of domestic underwriting capacity, and enhances confidence among India’s shipping and trade stakeholders. It added that extending the pool to include Protection and Indemnity coverage would further strengthen India’s maritime risk management framework and improve the resilience of its maritime insurance ecosystem.

. President Droupadi Murmu congratulated athlete Seema Kaliramna today on winning the bronze medal in the women’s discus throw event at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games 2026. In a social media post, the President lauded Kaliramna’s achievement, stating that it is a testament to her perseverance, dedication and hard work. The President remarked that this success would inspire young women to strive for excellence in sports.Vice President C P Radhakrishnan has congratulated weightlifter Lovepreet Singh for winning the silver medal in the men’s 110+ kg weightlifting event and athlete Seema Kaliramna for winning the bronze medal in the women’s discus throw event at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games 2026. In a social media post, Mr. Radhakrishnan stated that these achievements have brought honor to the country and will inspire countless young athletes.Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated Seema Kaliramna for securing Bronze medal in the Women’s Discus Throw event in Commonwealth Games 2026, with a best throw of 58.65 meter. In a social media post, Mr Modi said that her efforts have made India proud and motivated the youth of the nation. He wished her for the endeavours ahead.Prime Minister Narendra Modi also congratulated weightlifter Lovepreet Singh for winning the Silver in the Men’s +110 kilogram event at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, Scotland. In a social media post, Mr. Modi mentioned that Lovepreet’s outstanding performance in the snatch event set a new Commonwealth Games record. The Prime Minister further added that Mr Singh’s dedication and determination are truly admirable.

. Minister for Railways Ashwini Vaishnaw has said that safety is accorded the highest priority on Indian Railways and as a consequence of various safety measures taken over the years, there has been a steep decline in the number of accidents. In a written reply in the Lok Sabha today, Mr Vaishnaw said, after extensive and elaborate trials, Kavach Version 4.0 has been successfully commissioned on two thousand 569 Route Kilometres covering the high density Delhi- Mumbai and Delhi-Howrah routes as on 20th of this month. He informed that the funds utilized on Kavach works so far up to last month is three thousand 874 Crore rupees. Mr Vaishnaw said, the allocation of funds during the year 2026-27 is two thousand 66 crore rupees. He said, Kavach work is going at a good pace in the entire country. The Minister said, specialized training programmes on Kavach are being conducted at centralized training institutes of Indian Railways to impart training to all concerned officials. He said, by now more than 94 thousand technicians, operators and engineers have been trained on Kavach technology. He added that this includes about 57 thousand Loco Pilots and Assistant Loco Pilots.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended in positive zone for the third consecutive session today. The Sensex rose 166 points or 0.2 percent to close at 78,095. The Nifty added 66 points, or nearly 0.3 percent to settle at 24,384.In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index as well as the Smallcap 100 index gained over 0.4 percent.Earlier, markets opened on a firm note, and traded in a narrow range during the first half before gaining momentum during the afternoon session.In the Sensex pack, 16 out of 30 companies registered gains. Among the top performers, Bajaj Finance climbed 8.1 per cent, Bajaj Finserv rose 6.6 per cent and Mahindra and Mahindra added 3.6 per cent. In contrast, TCS and Eternal shed over 2.7 per cent, Infosys dipped almost 2.3 per cent and ITC lost one and a half per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 19 out of 27 sectors ended in positive zone. Among the top gainers, Auto advanced two per cent, Capital Goods rose 1.8 per cent and Industrials gained 1.3 per cent. In contrast, IT lost 1.4 per cent, Focused IT slipped 1.2 per cent, and FMCG fell 0.9 per cent.The overall market breadth at the BSE was positive, as shares of 2 thousand 568 companies advanced, 1 thousand 653 declined, and 204 remained unchanged.

Multiple earthquakes struck parts of China, Tibet and Nepal within hours early Friday, with the strongest tremor measuring magnitude 4.5 in China, according to the National Center for Seismology (NCS). The NCS said a magnitude 4.5 earthquake was recorded in China eraly today, at a depth of 10 km.Earlier, a magnitude 4.2 earthquake struck Tibet at 12:50 a.m. IST, followed by a magnitude 3.4 tremor in Nepal at 1:18 a.m. IST. The agency had also detected a magnitude 4.3 earthquake in Tibet at 11:25 p.m. IST yesterday.The four earthquakes occurred across the Himalayan region and western China, with recorded depths ranging from 10 km to 130 km. No casualties or significant damage were reported immediately. Authorities had not issued any emergency advisories or tsunami warnings following the tremors. The Himalayan belt is among the world’s most seismically active regions due to the ongoing collision of the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates.

. The death toll from the methane gas explosion at a coal mine in the Sorange area of Pakistan’s Balochistan province has risen to 34. The officials said that 41 miners were in the mine when incident took place. The powerful blast triggered the collapse of a large section of the mine, trapping several workers under the rubble. Local media, citing the Provincial Disaster Management Authority (PDMA), today reported that rescue operations are still underway to recover the remaining miners trapped beneath the debris.Chief Inspector of Mines Muhammad Atif said the blast was believed to have been occurred due to the accumulation of methane gas at a depth of around 4000 feet, causing a fire and gathering of hazardous gases in the mine. He stated that the majority of coal mine explosions in Balochistan took place due to the presence of methane gas.

. Union Home and Cooperation Minister Amit Shah arrived in Pune last night on a two-day visit. He will present the Lokmanya Tilak Memorial National Award to National Security Advisor Ajit Doval at a function in Pune today. The day marks the death anniversary of freedom-fighter Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak and the birth anniversary of social reformer Lokshahir Annabhau Sathe. Various programmes are being organised across Maharashtra to commemorate the occasions. After the award ceremony, Mr Shah will pay floral tribute at the memorial of Annabhau Sathe.

. An avalanche has struck an expedition on Broad Peak located in Karakoram range near K2 at an altitude of around 7 thousand metres, sweeping away a 10-member climbing team. Rescuers have recovered four bodies and continued search operations despite adverse weather. Nepal’s veteran mountaineer Nirmal Purja remained among six missing climbers.Broad Peak standing at 8 thousand 51 metres is the world’s 12th-highest mountain and is considered one of the most challenging peaks to climb. The climbers include- six from Nepal, one from Pakistan, one from Oman, one American and one Chinese.

. In Asian markets, South Korea’s Kospi index jumped 17.9 per cent, reversing its three-day losing streak amid renewed buying in chip stocks. Japan’s Nikkei 225 gained four per cent.Meanwhile, the Bank of Japan has left its policy rate unchanged at one per cent. However, in its outlook, the BOJ said that core inflation was likely to accelerate to a level above two per cent from the second half of current fiscal year.Major European indices were trading with gains today. Germany’s DAX rose over 0.3 per cent, and London’s FTSE 100 increased by 0.2 per cent, when reports last came in.Meanwhile, Euro area annual inflation rose slightly to 2.9 per cent in July this year, up from 2.8 per cent in June. According to a flash estimate from Eurostat, energy prices increased by 10 per cent on an annual basis, up from 8.5 per cent in June.

. The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) has extended the timeline for implementation of the revised Particulate Matter (PM) emission standards for industries operating across Delhi-NCR. The revised PM emission standard will now come into effect from 1st October this year. CAQM said that a limited extension of the implementation timeline would facilitate effective and uniform compliance by industries without compromising the objective of reducing industrial emissions.The Commission said, the revised PM emission standard continues to remain technically achievable and environmentally necessary for reducing industrial emissions and improving ambient air quality in the region. The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change said that the amendment is intended solely to provide additional time for industries to complete the necessary installation, retrofitting and assessment of air pollution control devices, while ensuring full compliance with the stringent particulate matter emission standards within the revised timeline.

. Five-time FIFA World Cup champions Brazil will play an international friendly against the Indian football team in Kolkata. The match is scheduled to be held at the Salt Lake Stadium on 3rd October. The announcement was made yesterday by the All India Football Federation.The Brazilian Football Confederation said that the country’s senior men’s team will first play two friendly matches against Australia. Brazil will face Australia in the first match at Townsville on September 25, followed by a second match in Brisbane on September 29. They will then travel to Kolkata to take on India on 3rd October .This will be the first-ever meeting between the senior men’s national teams of Brazil and India.

A delegation from Bastar Mandal of Chhattisgarh comprising winners of Bastar Pandum 2026, Pargana Manjhi and Chalaki of Bastar and Padma awardees, called on President Droupadi Murmu today at Rashtrapati Bhavan Cultural Centre. The President felicitated the members of the delegation and interacted with them. Union Minister for Home Affairs and Cooperation, Amit Shah, and Chief Minister of Chhattisgarh, Vishnu Deo Sai were present on the occasion.Speaking on the occasion, the President emphasized that events like Bastar Pandum have played an important role in reconnecting the youth with their traditions, customs, and cultural heritage. President Murmu highlighted that such events promote tourism and create employment opportunities. The President noted that the transformation in Bastar is a source of joy and pride for the entire nation. She expressed confidence that people of Chhattisgarh will scale new heights of development, peace and prosperity through their collective strength and determination. Further, President Murmu assured them that the government would stand by them in every situation.

. External Affairs Minister Dr Subrahmanyam Jaishankar has said that India has consistently supported the United Nations in strengthening international peace and security. In a written reply in the Lok Sabha today, Dr Jaishankar said, this support has been expressed in a variety of ways, including its unique contribution to UN peacekeeping operations. He said, this contribution is also reflected in India’s membership of the UN Security Council on eight occasions, with the next candidature formally announced for 2028-29. The Minister said, each tenure has witnessed placing issues of Indian interest on the international agenda, the most recent one, in 2021-22, focusing on maritime security and counter-terrorism. He said, the six priorities for the 2028-29 candidature are, A Voice of Global South, Advancing Reformed Multilateralism, A Future Ready Peacekeeping, Addressing threats posed by the misuse of AI, Securing Maritime Commons and Countering Terror Financing.Dr Jaishankar said India is a key contributor to global peace and security, with almost three lakh peacekeepers serving in more than 50 UN missions. He said, currently, four thousand two hundred Indian peacekeepers are deployed in nine out of 11 active missions, working in challenging conditions to promote international peace. The Minister said, India has firmly advanced its view that dialogue and diplomacy are the best means to achieve lasting and durable peace. He said, this has been stated in respect of the Ukraine conflict, the developments in West Asia as well as hostilities in the Gulf. Dr Jaishankar said, with regard to the challenge of terrorism, India has strongly advocated a policy of zero-tolerance and asserted the right of nations to defend themselves against terrorism. He said, since 1996, India has also called for the adoption of a Comprehensive Convention on International Terrorism.

. The Securities and Exchange Board of India, or SEBI, has clarified the rules for the sale of unlisted company shares. It said that if an existing shareholder sells such shares through a private deal to not more than 200 buyers in a financial year, the sale will not be treated as a public issue.The information was provided in a clarification letter issued to IDBI Bank, which had sought SEBI’s view on whether its proposed sale of unlisted equity shares to non-qualified institutional buyers through off-market transactions would be regarded as a public offer under securities laws.The letter published today says, these transactions are secondary transfers by an existing shareholder and do not constitute an offer or invitation by the company to subscribe to securities. The regulator further clarified that contractual rights such as the right of first refusal (ROFR) available to company promoters can be honoured while carrying out such share transfers.The regulator added that the transfer can be made through a non-advertised privately negotiated transaction to identified investors, including non-Qualified Institutional Buyer investors, provided the transfer is made up to the prescribed limit of 200 persons in a financial year, so it is not construed as a deemed public issue.

The government has said that the country became free from Left Wing Extremism after nearly six decades of violence, which was once considered one of the biggest threats to internal security.In reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha,  Minister of State for Home Affairs Nityanand Rai said that this has been achieved with resolute implementation of the National Policy and Action Plan to address Left-Wing Extremism 2015 and the coordinated efforts of Centre and State governments. He informed the House that at present, no district is categorized as LWE affected. Mr Rai added that the number of Naxal-affected districts reduced from 126 to 90 in April 2018, 70 in July 2021, 38 in April 2024, 8 in December 2025 and zero in March 2026.The Minister also informed that  at present, 37 districts are categorized as Legacy and Thrust districts, which are no more LWE affected, but continued support regarding security and development measures is required for some more time to consolidate the position. He informed that one district has been kept under the category of District of Concern where LWE violent activities have been totally contained and their organizational structure has been completely dismantled.The Minister said that in the post-LWE scenario, the focus is on saturation of government welfare programmes, strengthening local self-governance, facilitating the rehabilitation of surrendered cadres and expanding the reach of governance and public services in remote areas. Mr Rai said that overall, Centre is committed for ensuring security and accelerated development of erstwhile LWE affected districts of the country.
